name: Familial Avascular Necrosis of Femoral Head
aliases: Hereditary Avascular Necrosis of Femoral Head

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for familial avascular necrosis of femoral head

criteria.description: Presence of at least one first-degree relative diagnosed with avascular necrosis of the femoral head
Imaging evidence of femoral head osteonecrosis on MRI or X-ray
Exclusion of secondary causes such as corticosteroid use, trauma, or alcohol abuse
Presence of hip joint pain and limited range of motion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: positive family history, radiologic evidence of femoral head necrosis, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of the femoral neck or head region

searchTerms: loss of normal femoral head roundness

common.symptomName: Impairment of activities of daily living

laboratory: Exclusion of secondary causes by blood tests (e.g., lipid profile, coagulation studies)
imaging: MRI showing early bone marrow edema and necrosis of femoral head
X-ray demonstrating femoral head sclerosis, subchondral lucency (crescent sign), and collapse
genetic: Familial clustering suggesting autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Histopathology showing dead bone with empty lacunae and absence of osteocytes

distinguishingFeatures: History of hip trauma or fracture
Characteristic radiologic findings in pediatric patients

redFlags: Rapid progression of hip joint collapse
Development of secondary osteoarthritis at a young age
references: Orphanet: Familial avascular necrosis of femoral head - ORPHA:86820
